summary: Switched from periodic quotients to one induced subgraph of the infinite forced-offset Cayley graph at a = 1/5, pre-registered before computation: P = {v : N(v) <= 19}, 73 cells (N <= 21 would be 85 > 81, so this is the cap-respecting ball), 888 edges, max clique 4. CERTIFIED: the induced subgraph has no proper 6-colouring, so NO colouring of the plane constant on those honeycomb cells uses six colours - a whole-family no-go at this parameter, not a single-period one. Certificate: plain 6-colouring CNF (438 vars, 6496 clauses, no symmetry breaking), 42109-step DRUP proof, verified step by step by my own two-watched-literal RUP checker (rup.c/rup_verify, no drat-trim available), rc 0, empty clause derived. Also machine-decided: chi(G[P]) = 8 (two CDCL solvers 7-UNSAT; explicit 8-colouring with 0/888 monochromatic edges), so the family needs at least 8 colours at a = 1/5 - more than the plane's 7. The k=7 proof certificate exceeded the 60 s cap and was abandoned, so that stronger claim is uncertified. Two of my own tooling bugs found and fixed (watch invariant; unpropagated units). Retraction banner added to QUOTIENT16.md: the 'every 6-subset contains an edge' line is true but is NOT a chromatic obstruction; K_16 the clique is the valid argument.

verified_results.statement: At a = 1/5, forced offsets are exactly F = {v : N(v) in {4,7,9,12,13}}, |F| = 42 (re-verified exactly in Q(sqrt3) at the start of this block).
verified_results.grade: EXACT computation, third independent re-derivation in this directory

verified_results.statement: P = {v : N(v) <= 19} has 73 cells; G[P] has 888 edges, degrees 16..42 (centre degree 42 = |F|), max clique exactly 4 with witness {(0,0),(-2,0),(-2,2),(0,2)}.
THEOREM (certified): G[P] has no proper 6-colouring. Hence no plane colouring constant on the interiors of these honeycomb cells at a = 1/5 uses six colours; every one needs >= 7.
verified_results.grade: PROOF by machine certificate: plain CNF without symmetry breaking, 42109-step DRUP refutation ending in the empty clause, verified independently by a purpose-written RUP checker (rc 0). Producer and checker share no code.

verified_results.statement: chi(G[P]) = 8 (lower: 7-UNSAT by Cadical153 and Glucose3; upper: explicit colouring, classes 12,10,10,9,9,9,8,6, 0/888 monochromatic edges).
verified_results.grade: MACHINE-DECIDED, NO PROOF CERTIFICATE: the k=7 DRUP generation exceeded the 60 s single-process cap and was abandoned. Treat as a strong computational result, not a certified theorem.

verified_results.statement: No plane-colouring conclusion follows in either direction from this block; it is a no-go for one cell-constant family at one parameter.

Retraction: in QUOTIENT16.md the check that every 6-subset of the 16 cosets contains an edge is a true but insufficient statement (it gives only chi >= 16/5), not a chromatic obstruction; the valid argument there is the K_16 clique.
verified_results.grade: self-retraction, banner inserted at the top of QUOTIENT16.md

conjectures: chi(Cay(Z^2, F)) at a = 1/5 may be exactly 8, in which case no cell-constant colouring of the plane exists at this parameter at all (8 > 7 = chi(R^2) upper bound). Unresolved: needs either a k=7 certificate or a direct argument.

The cellular families excluded so far (hexagons for a in (1/sqrt13,1/2] and at a=1/5; squares at c=3/5) suggest small cells are the only place a cell-constant six-colouring could live, and that at very small cells the required colour count grows rather than falls.

failed_routes: My first sublattice enumeration used the lower-triangular HNF <(a,0),(b,c)>, which is NOT a complete list: it misses 6 of the 8 index-7 sublattices, including the paper's <(1,3),(0,7)>, and wrongly gave minimum index 8 at a = 2/5. Fixed to upper HNF <(a,b),(0,c)>; the control then gave 7 as it must.
The heuristic bound index >= ceil((1+D)^2/(3a^2)) = 17 at a = 1/5 was wrong (ring 16 escapes it); replaced by the multiplicative-norm argument giving 16, which the enumeration confirms.
A density argument (clusters of <= 4 separated by 1.3856) does not give a contradiction at six colours: 2.65 > 1.60. Recorded as a gap, not pursued further in this block.

A hand estimate that ring-16 cells could carry the N=16 forced offsets was wrong (ring 16 is unforced because dmin >= 1); it does not affect this block, where the window proof bounds N < 16.33 independently.

Carried forward and still relevant: the earlier lower-triangular HNF enumeration was incomplete (missed 6 of 8 index-7 sublattices); this block uses the upper HNF only, and the index-19 counts here are on that corrected enumeration.
p19_shrink.py: greedy UNSAT-core minimisation (73+ solver calls) exceeded the cap and produced no output; superseded, no core certificate.
k = 7 (i.e. chi = 8) DRUP certificate: generation exceeded 60 s; abandoned. The chi = 8 claim therefore rests on two CDCL decisions plus a verified 8-colouring, not on a proof.

rup.c first version had two real defects: clauses added with watches already false at level 0, and unit clauses enqueued but not propagated. The second produced a spurious RUP FAILURE; diagnosed with a naive independent propagation. Both fixed; the shipped checker is the fixed one.
patch19_proof.py: abandoned driver (pysat returns DIMACS strings, so its empty-clause assertion fired). Superseded by p19_gen.py.
Earlier in this block's lineage: the 'every 6-subset contains an edge' line in QUOTIENT16.md — retracted as a chromatic argument; K_16 is the valid one.
next_step: Two options, both bounded: (a) certify the k = 7 UNSAT for the same patch by shrinking to a smaller 7-UNSAT core first so the proof fits the cap — this would upgrade 'chi = 8' from machine-decided to certified; (b) apply the same 73-cell-patch method to one more a (the method is parameter-generic: rebuild F for that a, take the same ball, 6-UNSAT test plus DRUP certificate). Option (a) is preferable: it closes the only uncertified headline claim of this block.
escalation: Precise obstacle: the certified statement is 6-UNSAT on 73 cells, but the interesting claim (chi(G[P]) = 8, i.e. the family at a = 1/5 admits no 7-colouring and so no cell-constant colouring at all, since the plane's bound is 7) has no certificate because the k = 7 refutation is large. Definitions: G[P] the induced subgraph of Cay(Z^2,F) on P = {N <= 19}; F = {N in {4,7,9,12,13}}. Attempted: full-patch DRUP at k = 7 (exceeded 60 s), greedy core minimisation (exceeded cap), symmetry-broken CNF (valid reduction but shifts the proof burden onto a renaming lemma). Expected useful output: a 7-UNSAT core of <= 40 cells, or a symmetry-breaking lemma stated and proved so the smaller proof is admissible, either of which certifies chi = 8 within the cap.
